title: taken_over_row_is_excluded_from_the_sweep_test is insensitive to the taken_over_at clause it claims to pin — the row is excluded by the NULL clock instead
evidence: Test: "actions_handler.do_take_over(...) |> should.equal(200) ... rc_sql.sweep_due_reference_calls(db, "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z", 50) ... list.length(returned.rows) |> should.equal(1)" — the comment claims "the cadence SELECT never returns a taken-over row, even when the clock is due", but take_over_reference_call.sql:21 sets "next_attempt_at = NULL", so the SELECT's own line 58 "WHERE rc.next_attempt_at <= ..." excludes the row before line 59 "AND rc.taken_over_at IS NULL" is ever consulted.
detail: Deleting the taken_over_at clause from sweep_due_reference_calls would NOT turn this test red (the clock is never due on the fixture's taken-over row). The A7 sweep-exclusion invariant is pinned only in combination with the clock NULL, not per clause — the belt-and-braces guard ships unpinned.
recommended_fix: After do_take_over, set next_attempt_at = now() - 1 minute directly in the fixture (a hypothetical re-armed clock), then assert the row still does not come back; the test then bites on the taken_over_at clause specifically.
